questions.q: Why does ServiceNow ship Security Incident Response as its own dedicated application rather than having security teams just use the regular Incident table with a higher priority?
options: The regular Incident table cannot technically support a security use case
A security incident tracks something fundamentally different in nature than an outage, with its own legal, compliance, and investigative concerns a regular Incident never has
Security Incident Response doesn't actually use the task table at all
Priority fields are reserved exclusively for ITSM Incident records
questions.explain: The difference is in nature, not just severity — a confirmed breach carries legal and investigative weight a printer outage never does.

questions.q: What does Containment actually accomplish in a Security Incident's lifecycle?
options: It stops an active threat from spreading further, deliberately before the root cause is fully understood
It permanently removes the malware or root cause from the affected system
It restores the affected system to normal production use
It generates the final post-incident review document
questions.explain: Containment comes first and on purpose — stopping the bleeding now, even before the full picture is understood.

questions.q: Why is restoring a system to normal operation (Recovery) before Eradication is finished considered a real mistake, not just a stylistic choice?
options: Recovery and Eradication are actually interchangeable steps with no required order
Reconnecting a system before the root cause is removed just reconnects a still-infected system to the network
Eradication is optional and can be skipped entirely for most incidents
Recovery always happens automatically once containment finishes
questions.explain: Skipping ahead to Recovery before Eradication is complete undoes containment by putting a still-compromised system back online.

questions.q: What does Security Incident Response reuse from earlier in this path, per this lesson?
options: Nothing — SIR is built on an entirely separate, unrelated platform mechanism
The same task-table extension pattern covered in ServiceNow Scripting & Application Development, with SIR's own specialized workflow layered on top
The exact same state model as the regular Incident table, with no differences
The CMDB's relationship model, with no task-table involvement at all
questions.explain: SIR inherits task's core fields the same way any specialized table does — the specialized workflow on top is what makes it distinct.

questions.q: What is the real purpose of SIR's post-incident review phase?
options: It is purely a formality required before the record can be deleted
Structured learning from what happened, how it was detected, and what should change, so the same category of incident is caught faster or prevented next time
It replaces the need for containment and eradication on future incidents
It only applies to incidents that did not involve any real compromise
questions.explain: A regular Incident is done once service is restored; a Security Incident isn't really finished until the organization has learned from it.
